_comment: One planner action -> the sequence of sim text-actions that carries it out.
PEFA and FOLBP speak semantic actions ('[movetowards] <fridge>(40)'). Some of
them need several sim commands: the house demo's fridge is only openable from
a specific pose reached via two waypoints, its door is a joint link rather than
the object, and the flight to the terrace routes through a doorway waypoint.
Those waypoints are navigation detail, not decisions, so they belong here
rather than in the planner's action space -- a symbolic planner would never
invent 'flying_waypoint_out_livingroom_p1', and padding the benchmark's step
count with them would misreport it.
Keys are matched against the action AFTER the env json's name_mapping has been
applied, which is the form the bridge receives. Values are '<op> <target>'
strings, or ['<op>', [a, b]] for the two-argument ops. Anything with no entry
passes through untouched -- which is every action in the Merom demo.
Merom needs no macros at all; it is listed empty on purpose, so that an absent
task name reads as 'not configured' rather than 'nothing to do'.

A key may be scoped to one agent as '<agent>|<action>', which wins over the bare form. That is how the arm's grab becomes grabfrombasket while the dog's grab of the same object stays an ordinary grab.
